name: Two-Auxiliary Scale-Split Nonlocal F+ with Off-Ray Khronon Frame (TASSF+OFFRKF)
claimed_mechanism: This architecture enacts the mandatory scale-split theorem by using two distinct auxiliary scalars (chi, s) to localize the nonlocal F+ kernel: one auxiliary is massless to preserve the Coulomb pole required for the MOND force law, while the second is heavily gapped (m_s >> 1/a0) to freeze the spurious propagating mode without polluting the kernel. The preferred-frame lensing correction is mediated by a khronon field T with a standard kinetic term, ensuring the kinetic normalization is finite and independent of the screening factor. The e^-y screening applies strictly to the PPN-visible preferred-frame coupling (alpha_PF), not to the T kinetic term, thereby bypassing the P7 strong-coupling wall.
predicted_weak_field: In the weak-field limit, the massless auxiliary chi generates the standard MOND potential Phi_MOND. The khronon field T couples to the acceleration a_mu with a coefficient proportional to e^-y, generating a preferred-frame contribution to Psi that is distinct from Phi. Because the kinetic term of T is unscreened (constant canonical normalization), the sound speed c_T^2 remains O(1) and the strong coupling scale Lambda_sc is finite (set by the bare mass of T or the Planck scale), rather than diverging or vanishing with e^-y. This yields gamma_PPN=1 (correct lensing) with alpha_1, alpha_2 ~ e^-y (screened in the Solar System).
inequivalence_argument: This is inequivalent to DC-012 (frameless scale-split) because it explicitly includes a khronon field T with a preferred-frame coupling, which is the only off-ray escape from the slip-lock theorem (DC-013). It is inequivalent to the khronometric seed (SEED-KHRONO) because the MOND force law is generated by a spatially nonlocal F+ kernel (scale-split localization) rather than a local constraint, and the P7 collision is resolved by decoupling the screening factor from the kinetic normalization of T. It is inequivalent to DC-011 (single-mass pump) because the localization uses two auxiliaries with distinct scales (massless + gapped), satisfying the scale-split requirement.
